lesson_title: Zero Is the Only Number That Talks
hook_text: x² = 7x. You divided by x and wrote x = 7. Half your marks just left the room.
clip_script: Start from a money fact you already believe. A vendor's takings equal the price of one item times the number sold. If the day's takings are R0, either the price was zero, or nothing was sold. No third story exists. Takings of R80 explain nothing — endless stories. Zero tells one story. That is why every quadratic is pushed until one side reads zero before factorising. Now look at x squared equals seven x. Nearly everyone divides both sides by x and writes x equals seven. Not wrong — but not whole, because zero works too. Dividing by x quietly assumes x is not zero, and that answer lands in the bin. The safe route: x squared minus seven x equals zero. Take out the common factor: x, times x minus seven, equals zero. So x is zero, OR x is seven. Both kept. Never divide an equation by anything containing the unknown.
visual_style: A market till flashing R0 beside one flashing R80 with question marks swarming it; then an x tumbling into a dustbin and being lifted back out as x(x − 7) = 0 assembles in green.
pacing: Warm story beat on the takings, a sharp gasp at the bin, decisive rule to close.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and stop binning roots you already earned.
